review_scope: Read-only code inspection of B1 reader, frame-source linker, and operand route builder. No target run or tests were performed.

findings.observed: The reader does not first retain all JSON dictionaries. call_operand_reader.py:118-146 streams one bounded line; :177-188 parses one row and immediately decodes one typed event. However :175/:214 keeps a per-process event list, :222 copies its references into the aggregate events list, :224 makes a tuple copy for relationship validation, and :227-228 makes another tuple copy for the returned model. For the final process, the process list, aggregate list, and validation tuple coexist; the event objects themselves are shared references, not duplicated payload objects. Also :91-93 converts CollectingCallSink entry/exit lists to tuples without clearing the sink lists, so both pointer arrays remain alive through all sidecar reads and validation.
findings.complexity: O(E+F) retained objects, plus O(E+F) duplicate pointer arrays at peak; no O(E^2) JSON-row accumulation was found.

code.point: aggregate extend, validation tuple, return tuple

findings.generic_fix: Append decoded events directly to one aggregate list while maintaining per-process counters; after parsing, create one events tuple, pass that same tuple to validation and the result, and clear/release the frame sink lists immediately after transferring their records. This removes pointer-array copies without changing the raw protocol or event payloads.

findings.observed: _link_call_model with frame_scan supplied uses frame_scan.directory/files/captures/metadata and the passed entries/exits at call_edges.py:673-680, so it does not call _read_trace or decode the frame JSON a second time. It does rebuild entry/exit indexes and a sorted ancestry stack at :687-704. The reader already builds a separate ancestry stack for handshake validation at call_operand_reader.py:231-248; this is a second O(F log F) ancestry pass, not an N^2 pass. A separate concrete duplicate is that call_edges.py:669 calls inventory.to_dict() just to inspect schema_version, then :795 calls inventory.to_dict() again for its digest. ProgramInventory.to_dict at program_inventory.py:180-203 constructs the full inventory document, including files/bodies/frames and other present sections.
findings.complexity: No repeated raw frame read or per-entry JSON serialization in this path. Entry/exit ancestry is traversed twice in O(F log F). The complete inventory is materialized twice per model build.
findings.generic_fix: Read schema version from a cheap typed property/constant and compute the canonical inventory digest once. If the duplicate ancestry sweep becomes material, have the local raw-reader coordinator produce one ephemeral parent/invalid-interval index and pass it to the private linker; public replay must still rebuild that index from raw inputs.

findings.observed: build_operand_routes groups instructions once by invocation and builds per-invocation ordered index arrays at call_operand_routes.py:270-273. Attempts are traversed once at :295. _load_window uses bisect_left at :185 and checks only the call plan-sized suffix at :186-213. Gap/read-issue range checks are also binary searches (:174-176). Thus repeated attempts do not each scan the invocation instruction list.
findings.complexity: O(E+I+H+G + A log I_owner + sum(W_call)), where W_call is the narrow verified bytecode window per attempt. The attempt-to-instruction matcher is not quadratic in attempts or instructions.

code.point: binary search and bounded window check

findings.generic_fix: No fix is indicated for attempt-to-instruction indexing. A one-pass event partition could remove some temporary filtered tuples, but it is a linear memory/constant-factor cleanup only.

findings.observed: _instruction_plan calls dis.get_instructions(code) and rebuilds the complete offset-position map at call_operand_routes.py:139-144. _load_window caches plans by (code fingerprint, call offset) at :181-183, so repeated executions at the same site are cached, but every distinct CALL offset in the same code object triggers another full disassembly.
findings.complexity: For a code object with K distinct exercised CALL offsets and bytecode size S, preprocessing can cost O(K*S); if S grows with K this is quadratic in the number of sites. This is distinct from and does not make per-attempt instruction lookup quadratic.
findings.generic_fix: Cache dis.get_instructions(code) and offset-to-position once per code fingerprint within build_operand_routes; keep the existing per-(code,offset) verified window-plan cache.

findings.observed: _LightSource builds return_nodes_by_position in one ast.walk per source context at call_edges.py:168-178. returned_node queries that index at :397-407. _Core.return_root can call returned_node for each edge, but does not ast.walk the source file per return.
findings.complexity: O(AST nodes) index build per context and O(1) lookup per returned edge.

limitations: These are source-level complexity and object-lifetime observations, not cProfile results or measured costs on the newly running capture. No LeWM process was started.
